findings: shared/json-budget.ts treats an `undefined` value as unusable, so a TS object that spells an omitted optional field as `undefined` was reported as PACKAGE_BUDGET. Fixed by probing the JSON view of the package (which is what the store and the hash see) and keeping jsonWithinBudget semantics unchanged for wire values.

The frame needs `unsafe-eval` in its own CSP to instantiate compiled modules; the host CSP is untouched and the frame has an opaque origin with no cookie/storage/network (verified in the browser harness).

The bridge parser rejected messages containing `undefined` optional fields because jsonWithinBudget treats undefined as unusable; fixed by probing the JSON view on both the package and the message path, and by omitting absent fields when the host replies.
HTML5 drag-and-drop cannot be driven reliably by pointer emulation; the fixture uses pointer events, which is also the correct behaviour for touch and keyboard.

Independent review FAILED the candidate and found real defects; fixed in the follow-up commit: (a) a projection update arriving before the frame mounted was dropped — ports are now re-sent on frame load; (b) an inline `presentation={{…}}` remounted the frame on every parent render — the effect now depends on primitive fields; (c) a write declaration could target an `out` port — rejected now; (d) a behaviour module importing a pinned library passed validation and failed only in the isolate — all imports are rejected now; (e) the SDK promise could hang when the host dropped a message — intents now settle as abandoned on timeout and on the pending cap; (f) my own fixture encoded the wrong behaviour ABI (`{changes}` instead of a bare list).

Reviewer findings still OPEN (do not mark PASS): ISO-01 must be re-run from an http origin (downgraded to UNVERIFIED); the behaviour runner needs `behaviorId` + package-derived declared writes and must read `request.expected`, otherwise TOOL_STALE_REVISION/TOOL_SOURCE_REVOKED are unreachable; spec.md has no F080 entry yet; the frame runtime is ~685 KB inlined per instance and undocumented; the 64 KiB bridge bound is only enforced for string payloads; no CI job runs the tool-host harness; several declared limits/rejection codes are unenforced.

checks.name: single authoring pipeline (human + AI) with pre-dispatch budget and isolated trial
checks.evidence: 12/12: an over-budget estimate never calls the generator (the spy generator is never entered); no generator or no budget fails closed; validation → compile → trial → activation for both routes; one repair attempt receives the previous diagnostics; a trial failure blocks activation and keeps the problems; an unchanged hand edit is rejected as NO_CHANGE; the AI route is handed the person-edited base version, not the original

checks.name: authoring panel: edit source, check, activate, read back — in a browser
checks.environment: browser (system Edge headless locally, Chromium in CI) via file:// harness
checks.evidence: 8/8: the panel opens on the package with both source files; a syntax error is reported as TOOL_COMPILE_FAILED against ui/main.tsx and — asserted explicitly — never starts a pipeline run; fixing it activates with a readback of version, content hash, route=human, reviewer=manual and requester; a second edit produces a different content hash (so the pipeline used the edited source, not the original); the same job completes with the keyboard only; no page errors

findings: Budget enforcement is now structural rather than a log line: the generator is only reachable through a function that refuses when the estimate exceeds the remaining cap, which is what the paid-AI gate requires before any live call.

The panel check runs structure AND compile, because a syntax error is invisible to schema validation; without that the person would only learn about it after a failed activation. The refused check is asserted not to reach the pipeline at all.

The harness trial is a syntax gate over compiled modules, not an isolation boundary; isolated execution stays proven by the workerd runner tests (ISO-02). The panel is harness-only for now — mounting it in the app is still open.
tasks.nextAction: Mount the panel in the workspace UI (one entry point, one place that calls the pipeline) and wire it to the same authority path a real activation would use; the AI route stays behind the paid-AI gate.

checks.name: connection protocol: grant at the source, audience, effective revocation, in-flight adjudication
checks.evidence: 14/14 protocol tests: a read is authorized per port/audience/epoch; revocation is reported before a stale epoch so neither masks the other; the effective revocation point stops serving cached projections; an in-flight request is rejected when the grant was revoked or the source reset; the connection lifecycle is closed (revoked is terminal, missing is recoverable) · 10/10 grant command tests: epoch/dataRevision/issuer/time/version are stamped by the source (a client-supplied sourceEpoch or grantVersion is a payload error), duplicate ids and the live-grant cap are refused, revoke bumps grantVersion and is idempotent, and readGrantedProjection refuses after revoke/non-member/unexposed-port/stale-epoch

findings: REVIEW ROUND 2 (independent, verdict FAIL — correct): the authority calls assertIdentityFieldsAbsent on every command, so space.removeMember / space.setRole / space.transferManager / space.leaveSource were rejected with COMMAND_IDENTITY_SPOOF before the domain ran. My previous "space commands reach the command path" claim was therefore overstated and is corrected here. Fixed by extracting commandNamesItsOwnTarget() (precedent: access.assign) and exempting the commands whose payload names a target, with a regression test that also proves ordinary commands still reject {actorId}.

Also fixed in b4a94a0: a whitespace-only title was stored after trim and permanently wedged the workspace (now SPACE_INVALID); space/grant commands trimmed activity to 48 while the table keeps 100 (now one shared TABLE_ACTIVITY_LIMIT in helpers); a grant could name a resource/field the table does not have (now SOURCE_GRANT_PROJECTION); projectionUsableAt failed open on a revoked grant with no revokedAt (now fails closed).

OPEN review findings (do not treat the slice as closed): (1) readGrantedProjection takes isSpaceMember from the caller instead of deriving it from the space state; (2) space.addMember does not check the target is a workspace member; (3) adjudicateInFlight does not re-read the grant, so an audience/role change between read and commit is invisible; (4) joinedAt/epoch/sharedToolWorkspaceId are still client-supplied in space payloads; (5) revoked grants are never pruned (the cap counts live grants only); (6) there is still no CommandAuthority.execute round-trip test for any space/grant command; (7) the changelog fragment is stale.

Review findings 1, 2, 3 and 6 are closed at f09f327: (1) `authorizeProjectionRead`/`adjudicateInFlight` no longer take a free boolean — the caller must state that the destination verified membership, and an unstated claim is refused; the destination must re-verify before commit and the in-flight check now also rejects an actor outside the grant audience. (2) The authority validates the target of space.addMember/setRole/transferManager against real membership rows, so an outsider actorId cannot be written into a space (proven end-to-end: MEMBER_NOT_FOUND). (3) `server/space-commands-authority.test.ts` runs 6 commands through the real `CommandAuthority.execute()` on PGlite, which is the test that would have caught the blocker.

Still open: (4) joinedAt / epoch / sharedToolWorkspaceId remain client-supplied in space payloads; (5) revoked grants are never pruned so the array can grow; (7) adjudicateInFlight still trusts the grant object it is handed (the transport must re-read before calling it).
tasks.nextAction: Close (1)(2)(3)(6) first: derive membership from state, validate the added member at the authority, re-read the grant in adjudicateInFlight, and add one execute() round-trip test per space and grant command. Then the Room-to-Room transport.
